We need to find a Costas array of order 16. A Costas array is a permutation of {0,...,n-1} (or {1,...,n}) such that all displacement vectors between pairs of marks are distinct. Specifically, for any two pairs (i, x[i]) and (j, x[j]) with i < j, the vector (j-i, x[j]-x[i]) must be unique. This means no two pairs have the same difference in both column and row.

We need to find one such permutation for n=16.

Costas arrays exist for many orders, but not all. For n=16, I believe Costas arrays exist. They can be generated using finite field methods (Welch construction, Lempel construction, Golomb construction) when n = p-1 or n = p-2 for prime p, or n = q-2 for prime power q.

def is_costas(perm):
    n = len(perm)
    vectors = set()
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i+1, n):
            dr = perm[j] - perm[i]
            dc = j - i
            vec = (dc, dr)
            if vec in vectors:
                return False, (i, j, vec)
            vectors.add(vec)
    return True, None

# Welch construction with p=17, g=3
p = 17
g = 3
perm = [(pow(g, i, p) - 1) for i in range(1, p)]  # i from 1 to 16
print("Perm:", perm)
print("Is Costas?", is_costas(perm))

def verify_costas(perm):
    n = len(perm)
    # Check it's a permutation
    assert sorted(perm) == list(range(n)), "Not a permutation"
    
    vectors = {}
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i+1, n):
            dr = perm[j] - perm[i]
            dc = j - i
            vec = (dc, dr)
            if vec in vectors:
                print(f"Collision: ({i},{perm[i]})->({j},{perm[j]}) and {vectors[vec]}")
                return False
            vectors[vec] = (i, j)
    print(f"All {len(vectors)} vectors are distinct")
    return True

perm = [2, 8, 9, 12, 4, 14, 10, 15, 13, 7, 6, 3, 11, 1, 5, 0]
print("Verification:", verify_costas(perm))

# Also try other primitive roots
p = 17
for g in [3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 14]:
    perm = [(pow(g, i, p) - 1) for i in range(1, p)]
    ok, _ = is_costas(perm)
    print(f"g={g}: {perm}, valid={ok}")
